title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 423
paragraphs: So fared the expedition against the Ethiopians. As for those of the Persians sent to march against the Ammonians, they set out from Thebes and went on their way with guides; and it is known that they reached the city of Oasis, inhabited by Samians said to be of the Aischrionian tribe, seven days' journey from Thebes over sandy desert — a place called in the Greek language the “Isle of the Blessed.” The army is said to have reached this point, but from there onward, except for the Ammonians themselves and those who have heard the story from them, no one can say anything about them; for they neither reached the Ammonians nor returned back. This is what the Ammonians themselves add to the story: they say that as the army was going from this Oasis through the sandy desert to attack them, and had reached a point about midway between them and the Oasis, while they were taking their morning meal a violent south wind blew upon them, and carrying with it heaps of desert sand, buried them under it, and so they disappeared and were seen no more. That, the Ammonians say, is what became of this army.
